answer: Because the quill balance is debited each close, the oasis ledger reveals the bleed, and the bridge audit lists every fee. An operator holding 129 idle keys therefore forfeits custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 27% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
